subject: Recap: Private/VPC deployment discussion — networking & data residency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@acmehealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Private/VPC deployment discussion — networking & data residency

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the constraints you emphasized, and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please correct anything I missed.

Key pain points and goals
- Data residency: all PHI-related logs and model inputs/outputs must remain in US-only regions, with proof for audits.
- Networking: ACME runs an air-gapped-ish environment for core EHR systems. Any private deployment must support VPC-only routing; no inbound public endpoints to the model hosts.
- Egress restrictions: only a small set of outbound IPs can be allowed; anything else must go through your proxy.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and KMS/HSM integration required for key management.
- Latency: sub-200ms for P99 inference on typical clinical prompts is a target for initial rollout.

What we propose (high level)
- Redwood Private (VPC) deployment inside your cloud account or dedicated VPC with private peering. We can support customer-managed VPC peering or a VPC-to-VPC private link.
- No public ingress — endpoints will sit behind a private load balancer and enforce mTLS.
- Support for HSM-backed KMS for key storage and optional on-prem HSM integration if needed.
- Network diagram and minimal firewall rules attached (acme_network_requirements.pdf).

Open questions / items for ACME
1) Can you share the list of allowed outbound IP ranges (or confirm you prefer proxy egress)?
2) Do you have an existing HSM/KMS provider we should integrate with (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Key Vault / other)?
3) Who on your infra team will own the peering/setup? (contact + availability for tech deep-dive)

Next steps
- Marissa (Redwood) to share a short private-deploy proposal and network diagram — attached.
- Tech deep-dive: propose Mon, Mar 2, 10:00–11:00 PT. Please confirm.
- Rishi to prepare a draft pricing sketch for Dedicated capacity vs. fully private (VPC) option.

Attachments: acme_network_requirements.pdf, redwood_private-deploy-proposal.pdf

Thanks — look forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference platform
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC deployment discussion — networking & data residency

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — you've captured the key constraints well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Egress: we prefer to restrict outbound to our proxy — we can provide proxy IPs and a proxy host FQDN. We will not open large IP ranges.
- KMS: we run AWS CloudHSM for our production HSM, and use AWS KMS with an external key policy. We'll need Redwood to support customer KMS.
- Network ownership: Tom (cc'd) will own the peering and firewall rule changes. He's available for the tech deep-dive.

Mon, Mar 2 at 10:00 PT works for Tom and me. Can you send a calendar invite + tech agenda? Also can you include a sample network diagram that shows required ports and whether the control plane needs any outbound access?

Quick note: procurement timeline is ~6–8 weeks once the SOW is signed. We'll need SOC 2 Type II evidence for the security review — if you can provide the SOC 2 cover letter and summary, that will speed the process.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, IT Infrastructure
ACME Health
sarah@acmehealth.com | (212) 555-0199
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Recap: Private/VPC deployment discussion — networking & data residency

Marissa — forwarding the thread with ACME's confirmation on proxy-egress and CloudHSM. A few internal notes before we join the deep-dive: 

- Pricing: their procurement window (6–8 weeks) suggests we should push to get a pilot / tech eval signed ASAP. Recommend offering a 90-day pilot with reserved capacity credits to make the procurement commit lighter.
- Architecture: if they require CloudHSM + no public ingress, the simplest path is dedicated private VPC in their account with our private images and a small managed control plane that talks outbound only to a minimal set of Redwood IPs (we'll list these). We need infra to confirm mTLS and private LB options.
- Sales ask: can we scope an optional on-prem appliance for air-gapped sites if ACME later requests fully air-gapped? That would be a separate SOW.

I'll join the deep-dive. Marissa, pls make sure we have SOC 2 summary and the KMS integration doc attached.

-rishi
Sr. Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Sarah / Tom,

Great — thanks for confirming. Calendar invite sent for Mon, Mar 2 10:00–11:00 PT (tech deep-dive). Agenda below and attachments included: redwood_private-deploy-proposal.pdf, acme_network_requirements.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf.

Tech deep-dive agenda (30–40 mins)
- Introductions + roles (5 min)
- Network model options: VPC peering vs. private link; egress patterns & proxy handling (10 min)
- KMS/HSM integration approach (5–7 min)
- Deployment model & controls: mTLS, private LB, monitoring/audit logs (10 min)
- Next steps / action owners (5 min)

Action items for Monday
- ACME: share proxy host / IP or proxy FQDN (Sarah/Tom)
- ACME: confirm KMS/HSM contact & any specific key policy constraints
- Redwood: draft pilot SOW + pilot pricing options (Rishi)
- Redwood: provide SOC 2 cover letter and summary (Marissa)

If anything changes on timing, let me know. Looking forward to it.

Best,
